title: We used to
theme: Used to + would (past habits and states no longer true)
goal: Student uses "used to" for past habits/states and "would" for repeated past actions in narrative.
module_chunks: I used to + base / She used to + base
when I was a child / in the old days

units.title: I used to be different
units.real_life_context: You describe how things used to be in your childhood or before.

grammar.explanation: "Used to + base" for past habit no longer done.
Same form for all persons: "used to live".

grammar.sentence: We _____ go to the beach every summer.

grammar.explanation: After "used to", BASE form, not -ing. "Used to play".

grammar.passage: I used to play soccer every weekend. My sister used to dance. We used to go to the beach every summer. Now things are different.
grammar.question: What did the sister use to do?
grammar.explanation: The text says "My sister used to dance".

listening_speaking.text: I used to play soccer.

units.title: Used to vs Would
units.grammar_focus: Distinguish used to (states + actions) from would (actions only)
units.real_life_context: You choose correctly between both for narratives.

grammar.explanation: For STATES (be, have, like), use "used to", not "would".
For repeated ACTIONS, both work, but "would" is great with "every".
For "love" (feeling), use "used to". Not "would love" (which means "would like" in conditional).
For repeated past action narrative, "would" works (used to also works).
Repeated action with "every" — "would go" works perfectly.

grammar.sentence: She _____ be very shy as a kid.
I would have a red bike.
grammar.answer: I used to have a red bike.
grammar.explanation: "Have" (own) is state — use "used to have", not "would have".
"Like" is state/feeling — use "used to", not "would" (which changes meaning).

grammar.passage: I used to be shy. We would visit my aunt every Sunday. She used to live nearby. We would play games together.
grammar.question: Where did the aunt use to live?
grammar.explanation: The text says "She used to live nearby".

listening_speaking.text: She used to be tall.
Every summer, we would go camping.
I used to love that song.
My grandpa would tell stories.
I used to live in Rio.

units.title: Then vs now
units.real_life_context: You contrast past habits with present reality.

grammar.sentence: I _____ smoke, but now I don't.
grammar.explanation: Past habit no longer true: "used to smoke".

grammar.sentence: We _____ visit her every week, but now she lives far.
